environment.description: Same Ktor microservice deployed on EKS with Aurora PostgreSQL. The connection is established through RDS Proxy with IAM authentication. The database role 'app_service_ro' was provisioned via Terraform module 'aurora-restricted-role' which applies pg_hba.conf entry restricting the role, and the role itself was created with: CREATE ROLE app_service_ro WITH LOGIN; GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO app_service_ro; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_service_ro; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO app_service_ro; Additionally, a PostgreSQL event trigger logs and rejects any DDL. The RDS parameter group has 'log_statement=ddl' and pg_audit extension enabled with pgaudit.log='write'. Note: the Kubernetes ServiceAccount is annotated with an IAM role that has rds-db:connect permission scoped only to the 'app_service_ro' database user via resource ARN arn:aws:rds-db:us-east-1:123456789:dbuser:prx-0abc123/app_service_ro.

config.db_grants: GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_service_ro (no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE)
config.iam_auth: rds-db:connect scoped to app_service_ro user only
config.rds_proxy: Enforces IAM auth, connection pinning disabled
